item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q009_heme_bundle_fold_not_homology","answer":"No. In SCOPe 2.08, all three are in class f and share the heme-binding four-helical-bundle fold f.21 (sunid 81344), but SCOPe assigns them to three separate superfamilies: transmembrane di-heme cytochromes f.21.1 (sunid 81342), fumarate-reductase respiratory-complex transmembrane subunits f.21.2 (sunid 81343), and respiratory nitrate-reductase 1 gamma chains f.21.3 (sunid 103501). Thus SCOPe supports fold-level architectural similarity, not treating them as one homologous superfamily. The shared membrane-helical scaffold alone is insufficient evidence of common ancestry, so function, substrate specificity, interaction partners, or detailed heme chemistry should not be transferred among these groups. Cross-superfamily structures may serve as coarse fold-recognition templates, but homology-based modeling and representative selection should remain within the appropriate superfamily—and preferably the relevant family—unless independent sequence, structural, or phylogenetic evidence establishes a closer relationship.","evidence_used":["/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=transmembrane+di-heme+cytochromes","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=fumarate+reductase+respiratory+complex+transmembrane+subunits&limit=10","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=fumarate+reductase+transmembrane&limit=10","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Fumarate+reductase&limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=respiratory+nitrate+reductase+gamma&limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=nitrate+reductase&limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81344","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/f.21.2","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/f.21.3","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/f.21.1"]}]}
